tasks.short: Write fault, cause and action on the work order, note times and readings, type it into the maintenance system and update the machine logbook.

steps.what: Mechanic writes fault, cause and repair action on the paper work order

loop.input: The mechanic's voice note recorded at the machine, the work order's machine id, and the plant's fault and cause pick lists for that machine type.
loop.output: Draft action text and a suggested fault code and cause code from the pick lists.
loop.check: The suggested codes must exist in the pick list for that machine type; every reading, torque value and part number in the draft must appear in the transcript; the mechanic confirms or changes text and codes before closing.
loop.stop: One draft per note; if no code matches, the work order goes to the maintenance planner to code; on failure the mechanic types.
loop.why_not_simpler: Mechanics describe faults in their own words; pick lists alone lose detail and typed notes get skipped.

steps.what: Mechanic notes start, stop and downtime on the form
Mechanic records readings and checklist results from preventive maintenance
Mechanic types the paper work orders into the maintenance system at the end of the shift
Mechanic copies the repair into the machine's logbook binder
Maintenance engineer reviews closed work orders for repeat failures

tasks.design: Work orders are mobile in the plant's maintenance management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}): the mechanic taps start and stop, fills preventive checklists on the phone with a prompt on unusual readings, and speaks a voice note that a bounded step turns into draft text and suggested codes. Closing the work order is the record and the machine history; no retyping and no logbook binder.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper work orders were typed in later, often briefly, and copied into binders.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance apps transcribe voice memos into work orders and prompt on unusual readings.
tasks.still_hard: Time stamps per mechanic observe staff and need works council consent; codes must be confirmed, not accepted blindly.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what actually fixed it and saying so honestly.

ambition.what: Repeat failures reviewed every week from complete histories instead of once a year from binders.

tasks.altitude: The mechanic confirms a record instead of writing it twice.

reach.learn: Whether coded histories reveal root causes sooner.

evidence.claim: A maintenance app transcribes voice memos into the work order, drafts checklists for review, and prompts to confirm unusual readings.
Maintenance records software holds preventive plans and repair history.
A fibre network firm with 500 technicians reports about 8 hours per technician per week saved on work-order mail, entry and reports (vendor case, period not stated).
Work orders with time stamps can observe technicians and need works council consent first.

assumptions: Boundary: from the repair done to the machine history; failure analysis is outside.

Input contract: fault and cause pick lists kept by the maintenance engineer; checklists and reading limits from the preventive plans; machine ids from the asset register; fallback is paper work orders.
Times are used for downtime per machine, not to judge mechanics.
Engineer and planner time is outside the mechanic's savings.
unknowns: Work orders per mechanic per day.
Whether mechanics carry phones or tablets on the floor.
research_questions: How often do mechanics change the suggested codes?

already_counted.description: Mechanic confirms draft text and codes.

incremental.description: Mechanic learns the mobile work order.
Maintenance planner codes work orders with no matching code.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Plants with poor coverage on the floor, or no works council consent for time stamps, keep paper.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record parts used, find part numbers, check the storeroom, requisition missing parts, get approval, order from suppliers and flag low stock.

steps.what: Mechanic writes the parts or materials used on the work order
Mechanic looks up part numbers in machine manuals and parts books
Mechanic walks to the storeroom to see whether the part is there
Mechanic fills in a paper requisition for new parts or materials
Maintenance planner approves requisitions above the spending limit
Mechanic phones suppliers for price and delivery and orders the parts
Mechanic notices low stock of common parts and tells the storeroom

tasks.design: Each machine's parts list sits on its page in the maintenance management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with storeroom stock shown; parts are booked to the work order by scanning the bin label. Missing parts become a requisition from the work order, routed to the planner above the limit and then to a purchase order in the {ERP}; min/max levels raise reorders on their own, and urgent breakdown parts are still phoned.
tasks.previous_blocker: Part numbers lived in manuals, and stock and requisitions were on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems hold repair history and parts per machine and link to purchasing.
tasks.still_hard: Parts lists for old machines are incomplete; breakdowns need parts today, not via a form.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a part that fits when the original is no longer made.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; looking up and walking shrink.

reach.learn: Whether booked parts make min/max levels reliable.

evidence.claim: Maintenance records software holds preventive plans and repair history.
Scanning bin labels to book parts and min/max reordering are standard in maintenance systems.

assumptions: Boundary: from parts used to parts ordered; receiving is outside.

Input contract: parts lists per machine loaded by the maintenance engineer; stock and min/max levels kept by the storeroom clerk; spending limit set by the maintenance manager; fallback is manuals and paper.
Planner, storeroom and supplier time is outside the mechanic's savings.
Urgent breakdown parts are still phoned.
unknowns: Share of machines with complete parts lists.
research_questions: Does waiting time for parts fall once stock is visible?

incremental.description: Mechanic reports missing parts list entries.
Maintenance engineer completes parts lists for old machines.

approvals.approved_version: The requisition with part, quantity and price as approved by the planner in s5; orders under the limit need no approval; any change above the limit needs a new approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Plants with old machines and incomplete parts lists keep looking up by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear the symptoms, watch the machine run, test with meters, compare with expected values, note readings and test after repair.

steps.what: Mechanic hears the symptoms from the operator
Mechanic observes the operation of the machinery, watching and listening
Mechanic tests circuits and parts with voltmeters, gauges and other testing devices
Mechanic searches manuals and old notes for expected values
Mechanic jots measured values on scrap paper
Mechanic runs the machine after repair to confirm it works

tasks.design: The machine's page in the maintenance management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows reference values and past measurements next to the work order, and the mechanic enters readings there instead of on paper. Observing, testing and judging stay fully with the mechanic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference values were in manuals and readings on scraps of paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems keep repair history per machine.
tasks.still_hard: Diagnosis is hands-on; reference values must be loaded per machine.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the bearing that is about to go.

reach.learn: Whether stored readings show wear before failure.

evidence.claim: Maintenance records software holds preventive plans and repair history per machine.
The new machinery rules cover AI-powered safety functions, not maintenance records.

assumptions: Boundary: from the breakdown call to the machine released; the repair itself is outside.
Input contract: reference values per machine loaded by the maintenance engineer from manuals; fallback is the manual.
Observing and testing do not change.
Readings are stored per machine, not per mechanic.
unknowns: Share of machines with known reference values.
research_questions: Do stored readings shorten diagnosis on repeat faults?

incremental.description: Mechanic enters readings on the phone.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is hands-on testing, which does not change.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read error codes, look up their meaning, find similar past repairs, question operators, weigh the evidence and call the maker if stuck.

steps.what: Mechanic reads machine error messages on the control panel
Mechanic searches the maker's manual for what each error code means
Mechanic asks colleagues and digs through old work orders for similar faults

loop.input: The error codes, the operator's account as typed by the mechanic, and the machine type's closed work orders, including old free-text ones without codes.
loop.output: Up to five past work orders on the same machine type with the fault and fix, each linked.
loop.check: Every result must be an existing closed work order on the same machine type; the short summary of each must quote its own text; the mechanic opens and judges each one before using it.
loop.stop: One search per fault; no results means none shown.
loop.why_not_simpler: Old work orders are free text without codes, so a code filter misses most similar cases.

steps.what: Mechanic gets information from operators about what happened before the stop
Mechanic weighs test results, codes and accounts to diagnose equipment problems
Mechanic calls the maker's service desk about unknown faults

tasks.design: Each machine's error code list from the maker is loaded into the maintenance management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so a code shows its meaning and first checks at once. A bounded search finds similar past repairs on the same machine type, including old free-text work orders, for the mechanic to judge; questioning operators and the diagnosis stay with the mechanic.
tasks.previous_blocker: Code meanings were in thick manuals and past fixes in colleagues' heads.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintenance systems keep repair history per machine, and language models can match free-text descriptions.
tasks.still_hard: Similar is not the same; the mechanic must still test before trusting a past fix.
tasks.human_edge: Putting a vague operator story, a code and a smell together into the real cause.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; the mechanic starts with more information.

reach.learn: Whether past repairs help when no colleague is around.

evidence.claim: Maintenance records software holds preventive plans and repair history.
Language models can match free-text fault descriptions to similar past records.
Searching past repairs is not a high-risk AI use; it does not allocate work or monitor staff.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stop to the diagnosis; the repair is outside.
Input contract: error code lists loaded by the maintenance engineer from makers' documents; closed work orders from the maintenance system; fallback is manuals and colleagues.
Operator time is outside the mechanic's savings.
Questioning operators and judging do not change.
unknowns: How many old work orders exist per machine type.
research_questions: How often does a suggested past repair point to the actual cause?

already_counted.description: Mechanic opens and judges suggested past repairs.

incremental.description: Mechanic types the operator's account for the search.
Maintenance engineer loads error code lists.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Experienced mechanics on familiar machines rarely need to look up codes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The machinery mechanic keeps diagnosis and repair; records, parts look-ups and code searches shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A mechanic whose every repair leaves a complete, searchable history at no extra effort.
